title: The Umpire's Decision (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational cricket philosophy 102bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal absurdist sport
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The umpire raises one finger slowly toward the sky
And everyone within a hundred metres wants to know why
The batsman stares at a point somewhere beyond the boundary rope
The umpire has no doubt about it and gives the batsman no hope

[Pre-Chorus]
I once stood under a similar finger in the under fourteens
I walked before the word came — I knew what walking means

[Chorus]
The umpire's decision is final — this is known
Whatever argument you're making, make it on your own
The umpire's decision comes from somewhere deep inside
The umpire has been watching every ball and has decided
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The DRS review changed everything and nothing simultaneously
The third umpire sits upstairs and judges instantaneously
Ball-tracking and the hot spot and the snickometer agree
That sometimes what you thought you saw is not exactly what will be

[Bridge]
But in the park on Saturday at half past ten in August
When the umpire's in a hat and it's the third over in trust
Nobody checks the camera and nobody calls review
The umpire raises one white finger and that's the thing you do

[Outro]
Umpire knows… the finger says everything… umpire knows
That's my boy
